newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong continues climb, Bangkok regains ground.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong continues climb, Bangkok regains ground.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks continued their climb to record levels on Tuesday and Thailand's bourse, which lost nearly six percent after the weekend's election, bounced back on optimism over a new coalition government.
In Tokyo, the key Nikkei index added 0.77 percent in directionless trade.

Traders said Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index gained 14.13 points, or 0.11 percent, to post another record closing high. But it was well off its intra-day record high as a strong rally fizzled during the afternoon on fears of a share placement.
The Hang Seng Index closed at 13,056.93 after hitting an intra-day high of 13,183.01.
"There are just placement rumours around the market. If you get a bull market you generally get placements," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel.
"Despite all the warnings of consolidation, it looks like local funds and Chinese funds from mainland China are still buying," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.

"The China factor is still favourable and in fact it is turning more positive -- inflation is down in China and China assures us that the financial system in Hong Kong will remain intact (beyond Hong Kong's 1997 reversion to China)," he said.
Bangkok brokers said profit-taking during the Thai exchange's afternoon session curbed strong early gains but the SET Index still closed up 21.85 points, or 2.32 percent, at 964.19.
"It dropped off in the afternoon, there was some opportunity for profit taking once the market gained 30 points," said Barry Yates, head of research at the Multi-Credit Corporation.

The inclusion of Chart Pattana in a six-party coalition led by Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's New Aspiration Party (NAP) and news caretaker foreign minister Amnuay Wirawan was likley to become finance minister buoyed the market, Yates said.
Tokyo stocks closed higher after fluctuating in no particular direction on light trading volume. Shares of newly listed Deutsche Telekom traded heavily, but closed lower than the initial price.
The key Nikkei 225 average gained 159.81 points to 20,956.18.

Taiwan stocks surpassed Monday's 1996 record-high close at the finish on Tuesday, but last-minute profit-taking eroded gains from what brokers suspected was a politically inspired, state-engineered rally.
The weighted index closed up 28.16 points, or 0.42 percent, at 6,687.88.
The index was pushed higher by what brokers said appeared to be strong buying by state-controlled funds to mark six months since President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration.
President Lee was sworn in on May 20 and called at the time for state agencies to boost investment and show concrete results in six months -- about now.
At 1240 GMT, the dollar traded at 111.42/47 yen and 1.5026/31 marks, compared with New York's previous close of 111.50/55 yen and 1.5007/17 marks.
Hong Kong gold prices fell sharply to end at $378.40/378.90 an ounce against Monday's New York close of $378.80/379.30.
SIMEX Brent crude futures rose with the January contract last traded at $22.96 per barrel, up nine cents from London's close of $22.87.
